title: Line-Count Optimization Fallacy (Multi-Statement Jamming)
damaged_code:
```rust
// Rust
for i in 0..10 { a[i] = i; b[i] = i * 2; } // Jamming statements onto one line
```
pattern: Formatting multiple independent statements or complex loop bodies onto a single line to reduce the physical file line count.
why_bad: It does not improve compilation speed or execution performance. However, it severely degrades readability, forces horizontal scrolling, obscures compiler error line numbers, and prevents line-oriented debuggers from stepping through individual actions.
detection: A single line containing multiple semicolons separating distinct, mutating statements within a block.
counterexample: Empty loop bodies or trivial helper mappings such as `fn empty() {}` or simple unit test assertions. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Code Complete*, Chapter 25, "Old Wives' Tales" (p. 609-610) / *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 13.
